entry.quote: Also note that Tianxia was invested by Infinity Venture which is from Japan, this deal is not that surprising, I guess.

status_detail: DeNA took a majority stake in WAPTX Ltd. (July agreement, completed August 2009) and made it a subsidiary.
notes: TechNode 2009-07-03: DeNA 'has entered a tentative (not final) agreement to take a majority stake in WapTX, the owner company of the leading mobile SNS Tianxia'. Japanese Wikipedia (DeNA history): August 2009, acquired WAPTX LTD. shares, citing the MarkeZine piece 'DeNA、中国900万人が利用するモバイルSNS「天下網」の運営会社を子会社化'. The investment predates the e.ventures brand: it was made by Infinity Venture Partners, which became Infinity e.ventures (Asia desk) in 2012.

description: Unidentified company 'Xango', shown in the 2012 eventures.vc homepage carousel and later portfolio wall.
desk_reason: Inferred only: carousel peer of the Infinity (Asia) China logos (Rekoo, Yicha, WAPTX, Moca, Goyoo); no page ties Xango to the firm.
notes: Could not identify. Not the XanGo juice MLM (Utah). Google News (en, ja, zh), TechNode and TechCrunch searches found no Xango startup tied to Infinity or e.ventures.

The Moscow office invested from its own dedicated regional fund, not from the firm's main funds. TechCrunch (2012-07-15): before the rebrand the partners ran five funds, each under a different name, and the Eastern Europe fund became 'e.ventures Russia'. The firm's own boilerplate in HTGF's 2013-11-25 Torch release says it invests 'aus fest zugeordneten Fonds' (from dedicated funds): BV e.ventures (USA), e.ventures Europa, e.ventures Russland, Infinity e.ventures, Redpoint e.ventures. Russian deals credited to 'e.Ventures' predate the rebrand (Sapato $5M in 2010, Heverest $1.3M in 2011, rb.ru 2015-07-10). The Russian fund's pre-2012 name and its vehicle or manager entity were not found. Contrast: the US holding in Saatchi Online sat in 'BV eVentures Fund II, LP' (GP eVenture Capital Partners II LLC), and the Asia desk's funds were Infinity's own 'IVP Fund II' and 'Infnity e.ventures Asia III, L.P.' (Cayman), so each desk had separate vehicles.
quote: five different funds worldwide — in the US, Europe, Asia, Russia, and South America — each under a different name.
